recessive HYDIN mutations, which cause loss of the C2b CP-projection in respiratory cilia and sperm flagella, cause a PCD phenotype that is associated with normal body asymmetry and that is not associated with hydrocephalus.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of HYDIN as a PCD-associated gene and the identification of HYDIN mutations that cause PCD without randomization of body asymmetry.
the discovery of HYDIN mutations as a cause of PCD without randomization of body asymmetry, which has been reported in only one other PCD-causative gene.
the discovery of HYDIN as a PCD gene and the characterization of the HYDIN protein and the HYDIN gene product in cilia and flagellum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
recessive mutations of HYDIN cause PCD without randomization of body asymmetry.
HYDIN mutations can cause PCD without hydrocephalus, and without randomization of the left-right body asymmetries.
recessive HYDIN mutations are the cause of PCD in humans without nodal cilia dysfunction and randomization of left–right body asymmetry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HYDIN mutations are a novel cause of PCD, that HYDIN is a ciliary protein required for the normal structure and function of the central pair, and that HYDIN-deficient nodal cilia are not affected.
HYDIN is an important component of the CP apparatus of cilia and flagellum that is required for normal motility of respiratory cilia, sperm flagella and possibly also the nodal cilia.

HYDIN mutations are associated with PCD without hydrocephalus, and that the CP apparatus is essential for cilia and flagellar motility but is not required for normal nodal cilia-mediated left-right body patterning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HYDIN mutations are the first identified cause of PCD without randomization of body asymmetry.

HYDIN mutations are associated with PCD without situs inversus, that the CP apparatus is required for normal cilia and flagellar function and that, despite the absence of hydrocephalus, the CP is required for normal cerebrospinal fluid flow.
HYDIN mutations, which are not predicted to affect the CP apparatus of nodal cilia, are a cause of PCD without randomization of body asymmetry.
